newsitem.title: UK: BA surprised at any EU block to air deal.
newsitem.headline: BA surprised at any EU block to air deal.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Tuesday that it would be surprised if the European commission would tell the UK government that its proposed alliance with American Airlines will harm competition.
A spokesman also told Reuters that the European Commission has not discussed any concerns it might have over BA's planned link with American.

BA was responding to a report attributed to a European Commission source that the commission will tell the British government later on Tuesday that it has concluded that the planned link-up between BA and American would harm competition unless changed.
The BA spokesman said that the commission told it at the end of April that the commission had not finished its analysis of the competition issues associated with the proposed alliance.

The spokesman said, "In the commission's own words, this work will take some time to complete. It would be very natural for the commission to discuss their concerns with us before reaching a conclusion and this they have not done."

The European Commission said earlier that it had no comment on a meeting on Tuesday between Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert and British Trade Secretary Margaret Beckett on the BA/American plan.

The Commission announced in July 1996 it was probing several transatlantic air deals, including the one grouping Lufthansa, SAS and United Airlines, but none of them has been as controversial as the BA-American alliance.
--London Newsroom +44 171 542 4019
* The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 41.63 points to 3,214.28 points.
Bourse volume was at 1.96 billion francs.

One dealer said profit taking was nothing unusual after last week's record run. He added that markets are closely following the Fed's FOMC meeting. "But even the Fed were to raise interest rates, it would not be entirely negative, because it would help the dollar," he noted.
* Most-traded Novartis registereds fell 38 francs to 1,973 and Roche certificates were down 290 francs to 13,205. Nestle lost 39 francs to 1,818.
* Swiss Re, CS Group and Elektrowatt were among the few blue-chip winners.
* Swiss Re shares were up 10 francs to 1,834. The company said it expected a rise in 1997 net premiums of 20 to 25 percent.

Elektrowatt, in which CS Group has a stake of 44.9 percent, profited from a media report saying the spin-off of Elektrowatt's energy business may take place without the expected tax payment of 150 million francs.
A CS Group spokesman said the article was basically correct.
* CS Group was up 1.50 francs to 173.50 while Elektrowatt soared seven francs to 533.
* On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), activity was high in SMI futures and put options.

The drop in the cash market triggered a rise in implicit volatilities, dealers said. Total options volume was at 119,617 contracts with the call/put ratio standing at one to 1.20. Trade in UBS options was relatively high with 11,757 calls and 14,807 puts traded, one trader noted.
On the futures side, 30,181 SMI futures changed hands.
